VPC Lattice Is a Game-Changer for Service-to-Service Networking — But Beware the NAT Gateway Penalty
hook: AWS VPC Lattice has revolutionized service-to-service networking without load balancers, but our team encountered a unexpected surprise that added 30% to our VPC costs. Here's the hidden penalty that nobody warned us about and how we mitigated it.
angle: While VPC Lattice simplifies service networking, its lack of internet access by default can lead to a costly NAT Gateway requirement, undermining its benefits for some teams.
gotchaToReveal: The NAT Gateway penalty for Lambda functions running in a VPC without an internet gateway, adding unnecessary costs to the VPC Lattice benefits

title: The Hidden Cost of npm Package Bloat: How We Saved $10,000/month by Optimizing Our Lambda Dependencies
hook: As our serverless architecture grew, so did our npm package list. But when our monthly AWS bill skyrocketed, we realized that our dependencies were costing us big time. Here's the story of how we cut our costs by 70% with a simple package optimization technique.
angle: The unchecked growth of npm packages in serverless projects can lead to staggering costs, but a few simple tweaks can make all the difference. We're sharing our hard-won lessons to help you avoid the same financial pitfalls.
gotchaToReveal: The unexpected cost of npm package dependencies on serverless architectures, particularly when using Lambda functions.

title: TypeScript satisfies + AWS SDK v3: The Pattern That Changed How I Write Commands
hook: Last week, we migrated 12 of our Lambda handlers to TypeScript 5.5 and discovered the satisfies operator, which has changed how we write commands with AWS SDK v3. But what surprised us was how it affected our testing and validation pipelines.
angle: The satisfies operator in TypeScript 5.5 has revolutionized how we write commands with AWS SDK v3, but its implications on testing and validation have been overlooked. We argue that this operator is a game-changer for AWS SDK v3 command patterns, but its adoption requires a paradigm shift in how we approach validation and testing.
gotchaToReveal: The satisfies operator does not narrow the type at runtime, which can lead to unexpected behavior if not properly handled

title: ElastiCache Is Not a Silver Bullet: How We Fixed Node.js 22 Performance Issues with Undici and AsyncLocalStorage
hook: We thought ElastiCache was the answer to our Node.js 22 performance woes, but it only masked the symptoms. After months of frustration, we discovered the real issue – and the fix – lay with our choice of HTTP client and request context propagation.
angle: Contrary to popular belief, ElastiCache is not the solution to all Node.js performance issues, and sometimes, the answer lies in optimizing your code with the right tools and techniques.
gotchaToReveal: Undici's fetch throws on non-2xx status codes, unlike browser fetch, and AsyncLocalStorage context can be lost across setImmediate() boundaries in some Node.js versions

title: CloudWatch Logs Are Eating Your Margin: The $800/month Fix No One Tells You
hook: Developers rely on CloudWatch for logging and monitoring, but an overlooked setting is quietly bleeding away $800 each month. Our team stumbled upon this expensive trap the hard way and now we're sharing the simple fix.
angle: CloudWatch logs are a silent budget killer for many companies due to overlooked settings. Our discovery can save teams hundreds of dollars every month with a few lines of code.
gotchaToReveal: Default CloudWatch Logs retention period is set to 'Never expire', leading to significant and avoidable costs over time

title: Athena Query Performance Tanks After Migrating to Node.js 22: The Surprising Role of TypeScript Type Predicates
hook: We thought Node.js 22 would be a slam dunk for our data pipeline, but Athena query performance plummeted. It took us weeks to discover the root cause. TypeScript type predicates, intended to simplify our code, were secretly killing our database performance. Here's how we finally fixed it.
angle: The migration to Node.js 22 and the adoption of TypeScript 5.5's type predicates came with an unexpected performance price. Our story serves as a cautionary tale about the importance of thoroughly testing database interactions after significant technology changes.
gotchaToReveal: TypeScript type predicates can lead to inefficient database query plans if not properly optimized, causing significant performance drops in Athena queries.

title: We Replaced 20% of Our Lambda Functions with CDK Constructs — And Saved $12,000 on AWS Bills
hook: After weeks of refactoring, our team successfully migrated a fifth of our Lambda functions to CDK constructs, slashing our AWS costs and streamlining our architecture. Here's the surprising truth about what worked and what didn't.
angle: CDK constructs can replace entire Lambda functions, drastically reducing your AWS bills, but only if you're willing to refactor your entire approach to infrastructure as code.
gotchaToReveal: The little-known fact that CDK constructs can silently replace Lambda functions, but require a complete overhaul of your IaC approach to reap the full benefits.
